== Proposal: add P5137 (item for this sense) to lexemes by reusing an existing sense-link across a translation cluster ==

I'd like feedback before filing a BRFA on a method for adding {{P|5137}} ("item for this sense") statements to de/en/sv noun lexemes that currently lack a grounded sense. The pilot has been running as per-edit, human-approved [[Wikidata:Assisted_editing|assisted edits]] on my own account; I'd like to lay out the method and the licence rationale here for feedback before scaling up.

=== The idea ===

Many lexemes have forms but no ''meaning'' (no sense linked to a concept). P5137 is the established route to fix that. Instead of inventing a concept, I '''propagate an existing one''':

# Take a translation cluster from WikDict/DBnary (a set of lemmas that translate one another, grouped by which sense of each word the translation involves — not by gloss text).
# Find a cluster member whose Wikidata lexeme is '''already''' grounded via P5137 → some Q-item. Call that Q the '''anchor'''.
# Propose adding the ''same'' P5137 → Q to the other cluster members that lack it.
# An LLM does a single constrained '''yes/no''' check: "does this lemma denote ''this concept''?", judged '''only against the anchor Q-item's own label + description''' (Wikidata→Wikidata).

So the LLM never authors a concept or any text — its output is a verdict, and the statement written is a single bare P5137 link with a reference.

=== Licence rationale (this is the important part) ===

WikDict is built on DBnary, which is CC-BY-SA. Wikidata is CC0. The boundary is kept clean by '''what is used as evidence''':

* DBnary contributes only '''structure''' (which lemmas cluster — facts) and '''lemmas''' (facts). Both are uncreative facts, copyable to CC0 (cf. WMF Wikilegal on lexicographical data).
* The clustering uses each entry's own '''sense numbering''' (which translations belong to sense 2 vs sense 3) purely as a grouping signal. A sense ordinal is a factual index, not creative authorship — it carries no [[Schöpfungshöhe|creative height]] — and in any case it is consumed transiently and '''never reproduced''': the output sense link and its anchor Q are re-derived against Wikidata's own CC0 ontology, so no sense number, sense partition, or gloss is ever written to Wikidata. (A separate question — whether a ''dictionary's whole sense inventory'' enjoys the EU database ''sui generis'' right as a collection — is addressed below by keeping extraction sparse and non-republished, not by any claim about an individual sense number.)
* Verification is done against the '''anchor Q-item's own CC0 label and description''' — never the DBnary/Wiktionary gloss. No CC-BY-SA expression is ever read by the verifier or written to Wikidata.
* The output is a single re-verified bare P5137 link. The translation correspondence is consumed as ''evidence'', never republished — '''no translation property, no gloss text is written'''.
* As a guardrail against any EU sui-generis "extraction of a substantial part" concern, pilot/bulk volumes are kept modest and reviewed.

This is deliberately ''not'' a bulk import of a translation dictionary; it's per-statement grounding verified against CC0 data.

=== Precision (measured by hiding known links) ===

I measured precision by hiding a lexeme's known P5137→Q and checking whether the method recovers it (leave-one-out). To avoid flattering results, I separated out the ''cognate'' cases — where the two lemmas are spelled alike and the match is trivially easy — and report the harder non-cognate cases:

* '''Structural signals alone cap at ~81%.''' Using only structure — the concept confirmed by at least two independent grounded translations, a single-sense (monosemous) target, and a concrete anchor item — precision tops out around 81% on the non-cognate cases. Not enough on its own.
* '''The LLM verifier lifts this to 95.9%''' on the strictest slice of candidates, which I'll call the '''High tier''': an unambiguous lemma match, ''and'' the concept confirmed by at least two independent grounded translations, ''and'' a concrete anchor item (one carrying an {{P|31}} "instance of" statement). Pooled n=470; recall 94% (i.e. 94% of the genuinely-correct links are kept); 95% confidence interval ≈ [93.5%, 97.5%] — so the verifier ''alone'' sits ''at'' the bar, not clear of it (lower bound ~93.5%, and at a true rate this close no feasible sample size lifts the whole interval above 95%).
* '''Honesty check on ''fresh'' candidates''' — the actual writes: of 689 single-sense High-tier candidates the verifier accepted '''51%''', rejected 33%, and was uncertain on 16%. The rejections are correct catches — e.g. a feminine demonym wrongly clustered onto a ''language'' item rather than the ''people'' concept. Fresh candidates are harder than the held-out test, and the verifier is doing real work exactly there.
* '''Direct precision on the fresh stream''' — the human review ''does'' provide an answer for the verifier-accepted candidates: of 188 verifier-"yes" High-tier candidates reviewed so far, 180 were confirmed correct = '''95.7%''' (Wilson 95% CI [91.8%, 97.8%]). This is measured on the real write stream, not the held-out set, and it agrees with the held-out 95.9%. (Caveat: a single reviewer, and the verifier and reviewer are not independent — both judge from the same CC0 description.)

The High tier is ~7,400 candidate statements across de/en/sv; applying the measured 51% accept-rate, ~3,800 would be proposed for human review.

But the verifier rate is deliberately ''not'' the safety mechanism. In the pilot and the proposed trial, '''every edit is individually confirmed by a human against the anchor's CC0 description before it is written''' — so output precision is governed by that per-edit review, not by the verifier's statistical hit-rate. The 95.9% / 95.7% figures are reported for transparency (how good the verifier-accepted stream is), to show the human is checking a stream that is already mostly correct rather than rubber-stamping noise. 2-of-3 verifier voting could push the verifier-only rate higher, but given the per-edit human gate it is optional, not load-bearing.

=== External context: automated sense-linking is hard (why the human gate matters) ===

To situate the verifier — and to explain why the '''human gate''', not the verifier's statistical hit-rate, is the safety mechanism — automated word-sense linking is an open, hard problem:

* State-of-the-art WSD reaches only ~80 F1 on the standard English all-words benchmark and '''collapses on hard / out-of-distribution instances''': a gold-trained system scores 0.0, and even a 685-billion-parameter LLM manages only ~50 F1 on the HardEN set — instances that no prior system disambiguated correctly ([https://aclanthology.org/2025.emnlp-main.45/ Ming, Zhong & Li, EMNLP 2025]).
* When the "candidate senses are given" assumption is dropped and a system must both find the spans ''and'' link them end-to-end (closer to this setting), the best reported result is ~76 F1 ([https://aclanthology.org/2024.findings-acl.851/ Bejgu et al., Findings of ACL 2024]).

The verifier is therefore deliberately '''not''' run unsupervised. The pipeline (a) restricts to high-confidence, concrete-referent candidates; (b) classifies the sense↔item relation on a graded '''EQUAL / BROADER / NARROWER / LATERAL''' scale — the ontological-proximity scoring that recent surveys recommend over exact sense-match ([https://doi.org/10.3390/e28020236 Simos & Makris, ''Entropy'' 2026]); and (c) writes only '''human-confirmed EQUAL''' links. Using an LLM to filter candidate sense-links is itself an established technique in recent WSD-corpus construction (LLM-as-judge). None of these numbers is a like-for-like precision baseline for our stream — different inventory (WordNet vs Wikidata items), task (disambiguate every token vs verify one filtered link), and metric (exact-match F1 vs graded precision under a human gate) — they are cited as ''context'' for why the gate is load-bearing, not as a bar we claim to clear.

=== What gets ''declined'' (reviewer discipline) ===

P5137 asserts the sense ''denotes that exact concept'', so the bar is equality, not similarity. Worked rules I apply (and which a reviewer can audit):

* '''Near-synonym / hypernym / hyponym → abstain.''' e.g. ''Zwielicht'' (dim light, possible with the sun up) → "twilight" (defined by the sun being ''below'' the horizon) is a superset mismatch → declined.
* '''Abstract qualities/traits → out of the concrete-noun pilot''' (e.g. "advantage", "determination"), while precise non-physical count/event nouns are fine (e.g. "canonization", "specialized term").
* '''Register gate''': if the anchor item is itself modelled as pejorative/slang, the target must share that register.
* '''Demonyms''': the anchor must be the ''people'' concept, never the language or the continent.
* '''Biological common names''' anchor at the taxon rank the word denotes (cactus = family, dog = species).

=== Reference scheme ===

Every statement carries a mandatory reference — never bare:
* {{P|887}} (based on heuristic) → [[Q140308675]] "inferred from translation" (a purpose-made heuristic item; {{P|31}} → heuristic)
* {{P|813}} (retrieved) → date

The edit summary discloses the inferred-from-translation + LLM-verified + human-approved nature of each edit. No lineage that would republish DBnary's structure (source languages/translations) is recorded — that stays off-wiki.

=== Live examples (assisted edits, on my account) ===

A first per-edit-approved batch is live, each hand-checked against the anchor's CC0 description:
* ''Aar'' (de) → [[Q2092297]] (eagle) — [[Special:Diff/2508825516]]
* ''Beutelwolf'' (de) → [[Q123102]] (thylacine) — [[Special:Diff/2508826923]]
* ''Blattlaus'' (de) → [[Q183350]] (aphid) — [[Special:Diff/2508826930]]
* ''Asiat''/''Asiatin'' (de) → [[Q4058325]] (Asian people) — same neutral people-concept for both gendered forms

=== What I'm asking ===

# Is the CC0 licence boundary (verify against the anchor's own CC0 label/description; never the DBnary gloss; write only a bare referenced P5137) sound as described?
# Is the P887 → [[Q140308675]] reference scheme the right way to disclose the heuristic, or is a different reference preferred?
# Any objection to me filing a BRFA for a 50–250-edit trial on the High tier, single-sense targets first (adding to an existing sense; sense-''creation'' deferred pending a gloss-source decision)?

Thanks — happy to share the full method write-up, the precision harness, and per-case verdicts.
